calls.price_at_call: ~$128 (stated, below $135 IPO price); DCF fair value $95
calls.thesis: FLIP: was AVOID 8 Nov, now HOLD / market perform (his tracker rating) — first DCF on SpaceX gives FV $95 vs ~$128, still ~25% above his value, so 'not a buying opportunity' and he personally would not buy at $127, but no longer an avoid after the sharp sell-off; for investors very bullish on Musk it could be a reasonable buy. SpaceX sold $32B of bonds at 8.259% yield to fund Nvidia chip purchases, pivoting to renting compute (Neo Cloud) as its own AI model trails OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini in 4th/5th place.
calls.base_case: Huge forecast growth: free cash flow from ~$48B in 2029 to $656B by 2035; stock-market investors will keep funding the company.
calls.bull_case: Neo Cloud rental revenue reaches $10-30B annually; Musk delivers on forecasts at a better rate than his ~2-3/10 track record.
calls.bear_case: Bond market charges a hefty premium (8.259% vs 5.95% average investment-grade); capex dwarfs cash generation and the story depends on future investment; Musk's forecasts historically overpromise.
calls.video_title: This Dip Might Be Your Best Chance to Buy SpaceX Stock at a Reasonable Price

calls.thesis: AVOID — FLIP from HOLD (24 Oct; 28 Oct UNCERTAIN was passing opinion only). SpaceX overvalued (less so than Tesla); merger with Tesla faces a much tougher regulatory road after Democrats won the Texas Senate, governor and AG seats.
calls.base_case: Data-centre rental revenue (Alphabet, Anthropic) slows if build-out is restricted.
calls.bull_case: Merger still happens in 2027 despite the tougher roadmap (Dan Ives view, which he disputes).
calls.bear_case: Regulators block the merger; valuation compresses.

calls.video_title: Is SpaceX Stock a Buy After Reporting Spectacular Earnings Results?
calls.thesis: HOLD, low conviction, first explicit SPCX call for Parkevtate (prior mention was UNCERTAIN in a GOOG video, so no flip) — SpaceX is one of the most exciting stocks in the market, but at 63x price-to-sales the valuation is still too rich to rank it a buying opportunity; he would wait for a better entry point.
calls.base_case: Revenue $14.6bn, up 161%, with $2.8bn operating profit versus losses a year ago; the space segment was relatively flat, which he calls lumpy rather than a concern, and the company launched its first revenue-generating Starship flight in the period covered.
calls.bull_case: Starlink is sustainably attractive: subscribers nearly doubled to 13.6m from 7.2m, connectivity revenue rose to $5.2bn from $3.1bn with $2.4bn operating income (over 40% margin) at $69 average revenue per user; the superintelligence segment jumped to $7.56bn from $813m by renting compute to customers including Alphabet and Anthropic.
calls.bear_case: Capital spending dwarfs cash generation — capex $48bn in the first nine months of 2026 vs $13.1bn cash flow from operations — and superintelligence capex alone was $16.4bn in the quarter; at 63x sales much of the price is an Elon Musk premium that could evaporate quickly, and its own AI model ranks only fourth or fifth behind OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini.
